subject: Biology
title: Cancer as Evolution Inside the Body
description: A quick, practical guide to Cancer as Evolution Inside the Body.

hook.text: Cancer is natural selection happening inside your body—mutant cells competing for resources.

buildup.text: Cancer cells accumulate mutations that let them grow faster, dodge immune cells, and recruit blood vessels.

discovery.text: Tumors are diverse populations—different clones compete, and the fittest clones expand.

twist.text: Chemotherapy kills susceptible cells but selects for resistant ones—an evolutionary arms race inside a patient.

climax.text: Adaptive therapy gives lower drug doses to keep drug-sensitive cells alive—they outcompete resistant ones.

punchline.text: Cancer evolves. Treatment must evolve with it.

quiz.question: Why can chemotherapy sometimes fail over time?
options: It selects for drug-resistant cancer cell clones
The drugs expire inside the body
The patient becomes immune to the drug

details.summary: Cancer is essentially evolution occurring within the body. Tumor cells accumulate mutations, face selection pressures from the immune system and treatment, and evolve drug resistance through the same principles of variation, selection, and inheritance that drive species evolution.
details.whyItMatters: Viewing cancer as an evolutionary process explains why it is so hard to cure. Tumors are heterogeneous populations that evolve rapidly, and treatment resistance emerges through natural selection among cancer cells.
takeaways: Tumors contain diverse cell populations that compete and evolve
Chemotherapy selects for resistant cells, driving treatment failure
Adaptive therapy aims to manage rather than eliminate tumor evolution

faq.question: How does chemotherapy drive cancer evolution?
faq.answer: Chemotherapy kills sensitive cells but spares rare resistant mutants. With competition removed, resistant cells proliferate and dominate the tumor. This is exactly like antibiotic resistance in bacteria, natural selection favoring the survivors.

faq.question: What is adaptive therapy for cancer?
faq.answer: Instead of maximum-dose treatment aiming to kill all cancer cells, adaptive therapy uses lower doses to maintain a population of drug-sensitive cells that compete with resistant ones. This evolutionary approach aims to delay resistance emergence.
